reason: The cited evidence (E1) shows FSP on high-entropy alloys, not nickel-based superalloys, and does not address hot cracking, wear, or corrosion resistance. E2 discusses grain boundary serration in a different alloy system and processing route (SLM), not FSP. Thus, none of the key premises specific to nickel-based superalloys are supported by the cited passages.
premises: FSP can be applied to nickel-based superalloys to refine surface microstructure
FSP induces dynamic recrystallization forming fine, equiaxed grains with reduced microsegregation
FSP eliminates casting/welding defects and reduces residual stress
Refined microstructure enhances resistance to hot cracking, wear, and corrosion
Optimized FSP parameters (e.g., 800-1200 rpm, 20-40 mm/min) yield these improvements
